column1: CP1Intent formulationExpress the evaluative intent C as the operational judgement required by the source engineering concern, without introducing sensors, variables, representation mechanisms, or failure modes not required by that concern.

CP2Phenomenon identificationDefine the Phenomenon of Interest P as the operational condition about which C makes a judgement rather than as the telemetry, model, sensor output, computation, control mechanism, or other representation through which that condition is observed or maintained. P may be relational when the judgement depends on relationships among operational entities or conditions.

CP3Dimension admissibilityAdmit an evaluation dimension only when (i) the contrasted situations are states of the Phenomenon of Interest established in RR2, and (ii) variation along that dimension can be traced to visible engineering artefacts as potentially changing the judgement expressed by C. A requirement constraining an observation, computation, communication, or control mechanism does not by itself establish a CRD of P, even when violation of that requirement may affect the evaluation.

CP4Minimal contrastConstruct contrasting situations by varying the evaluation dimension under analysis while holding other relevant conditions stable where the available artefacts permit this, avoiding implementation-specific differences that are not required by C.

CP5Collapse testRecord a contrast as a Concern-Relevant Distinction only when making its contrasted classes indistinguishable would remove information required to evaluate C; operational difference alone is insufficient.

CP6Reference translationDo not treat downstream hazards, failure modes, fault-tree events, or execution failures directly as CRDs. First classify downstream evidence as phenomenon-level distinction evidence, a preservation/dependency threat, or an execution/control failure. Translate it into a reference CRD only when the documented evidence establishes a distinction between states of P required by C.

CP7AbstractionRepresent contrasts at the most general level supported by the evaluative intent and visible artefacts. Merge instance-specific contrasts, operational determinants, or failure mechanisms when they impose the same preservation obligation and no visible requirement requires them to remain separately distinguishable.
CP8SeparationKeep contrasts separate when they support different evaluative judgements, correspond to explicitly required categories, or require different distinguishability criteria.

CP9Semantic matchingMatch a RAISE2 distinction to a reference distinction according to the operational contrast and its role in evaluating C, rather than lexical similarity, shared components, or common failure mechanisms.

CP10Unsupported derivationDo not classify a derived distinction as unsupported solely because it is absent from the held-out reference artefacts. Classify it as unsupported only when neither the reference set nor the visible source artefacts provide a traceable rationale showing why its collapse would impair evaluation of C.

CP11Phenomenon--representation separationDo not introduce a contrast into D_C solely because two observation, representation, computation, or control states differ. The contrasted situations must differ in P in a manner relevant to C; failures of mechanisms used to observe, represent, compute, communicate, or control P are considered separately when assessing preservation and dependencies.

CP12Temporal scopeA temporal contrast is admissible only when the timed property belongs to P and its temporal evolution is required by C. Timing constraints on mechanisms used to observe, compute, communicate, or control P are treated as dependencies, assumptions, revalidation conditions, or preservation threats unless the source artefacts establish the timed behaviour itself as part of P.
